overview: After the Accelerated Panov move order 2.c4 d5, White plays 3.e5 instead of exchanging on d5. Black can take on c4 and keep a pawn, while White hopes for space and quick development. It is a rare anti-Caro-Kann idea and I am unsure of the usual follow-up.

white_ideas.idea: Gain space with e5 and develop with Nc3 and Bxc4-type recaptures
Seek a lead in development for the pawn

black_ideas.idea: Take 3...dxc4 and hold the extra pawn, then hit e5 with ...Nc6 and ...Bf5

typical_structures.structure: White e5/d4 wedge against Black c6/e6

character.notes: A pawn-down space grab with open lines for both.

gambit.notes: 3...dxc4 wins a pawn that Black can try to keep.

soundness.notes: Black appears to be a clean pawn up with a solid structure, so White is risking more than Black.

structure.notes: Advance-like pawn chain with the c-pawn gone from the centre.

level.notes: Needs judgement of compensation, little to memorise.

sublines_that_differ.name: Black declines with 3...Bf5
sublines_that_differ.how: No pawn is given; transposes to Advance-like play.

character.reason: A rare gambit but not a forcing attack; the position is unclear without being sharply tactical.

gambit.reason: White offers the c4 pawn for space and development.

soundness.reason: Black can keep the pawn with a solid centre, so the gambit leans on surprise.

structure.reason: White gets an e5 wedge while the c-file opens for Black.

approach.reason: This anti-Caro-Kann gambit is seldom seen at higher levels.

level.reason: A dubious gambit is not a first repertoire line.

plans.reason: White trades a pawn for space and speed.
